guide_enrichment.narrative:
What stands out to us is how closely the market already reflects our overall view. Wake Forest’s opener showed legitimate offensive upside: the offense produced 559 yards, while Gio Lopez threw for 350 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. We also saw an offensive line that did not allow a sack. Still, we are treating that performance against Akron as context rather than proof that the same efficiency will carry into a substantially more difficult matchup.

For us, the main constraint is Wake Forest’s ability to sustain drives against a Miami defense our longer-run numbers rate favorably against both the pass and the run. Miami also holds a clear numerical advantage in preventing scoring opportunities, which matters when the market is asking Wake Forest to remain competitive for four quarters. Wake Forest generated touchdown passes of 78 and 72 yards in its opener, but relying on explosive plays is different from consistently creating quality possessions. We do not see enough separation between our expectation and the market’s to justify a position.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Wake Forest’s passing offense against Miami’s pass defense. Lopez’s debut was efficient and explosive, but our numbers identify this as the clearest area in which Miami can disrupt what worked in the opener. The question for us is whether Wake Forest can stay efficient when explosive completions are harder to find.

We will also be watching protection closely. Wake Forest kept Lopez clean against Akron, but maintaining that stability is important because the passing matchup already leans toward Miami in our numbers. If Wake Forest cannot create manageable situations through the air, its path to staying inside the market expectation becomes considerably narrower.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest opened the 2026 season with a 38-16 home victory over Akron on Sept. 3.
Wake Forest produced 559 total yards against Akron, including 356 passing yards and 203 rushing yards.
Wake Forest committed no turnovers and gained one turnover against Akron.
Wake Forest converted 7 of 15 third downs and both of its fourth-down attempts against Akron.
Wake Forest allowed Akron 305 total yards, including 149 rushing and 156 passing, while recording seven tackles for loss and two sacks.

quarterback.fact: North Carolina transfer Gio Lopez is Wake Forest's starting quarterback and one of six team captains.
In his Wake Forest debut against Akron, Lopez completed 21 of 32 passes for 350 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions while adding 39 rushing yards.
Lopez's 78-yard touchdown pass to Carlos Hernandez against Akron was the longest completion of his collegiate career.
Through the Akron game, Lopez's career totals were 438 completions in 666 attempts for 5,131 yards, 35 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, plus 791 rushing yards and 12 rushing touchdowns.
Lopez previously played under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell at South Alabama.

offensive_personnel.fact: Wide receiver Carlos Hernandez caught five passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against Akron and added 18 punt-return yards.
Hernandez has caught at least five passes in each of his last five games, averaging 107.6 receiving yards with five touchdowns during that span.
Running back Ty Clark III rushed seven times for a career-high 105 yards against Akron, including a career-long 57-yard run.
Antonio Meeks recorded 93 receiving yards against Akron, while Kam Shanks caught five passes.
Wake Forest's unofficial depth chart lists Carlos Hernandez, Antonio Meeks and Kam Shanks as the first-team wide receivers, with Ty Clark III at running back.
The unofficial depth chart lists Will Loerzel, Landon Morris, Kamrean Johnson and freshman Dominick Barry as options at tight end.

defensive_personnel.fact: Wake Forest's six captains include defensive lineman Langston Hardy, linebacker Aiden Hall and defensive back Davaughn Patterson.
Aiden Hall became a starter in 2025 and finished that season with 73 tackles, eight tackles for loss and three passes defensed.
Against Akron, Vincent Firenze and Frank Cusano each recorded nine tackles; Firenze also forced a fumble.
Rushaun Tongue recovered Wake Forest's forced fumble against Akron.
Braylon Johnson recorded one sack against Akron, while Gabe Kirschke and Dallas Afalava each recorded 1.5 tackles for loss.
The unofficial depth chart lists Langston Hardy, Dallas Afalava, Zach Lohavichan and Gabe Kirschke across the starting defensive front.

coaching_changes.fact: Jake Dickert is in his second season as Wake Forest's head coach after being hired on Dec. 18, 2024.
Rob Ezell is Wake Forest's offensive coordinator, Dan Enos is co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach, and Jared Kaster coaches the offensive line.
Scottie Hazelton is Wake Forest's defensive coordinator, and Freddie Banks is co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
Dyrell Roberts joined Wake Forest as wide receivers coach in 2026 after coaching East Carolina's receivers from 2023 through 2025.

offensive_context.fact: Wake Forest did not allow a sack against Akron.
Wake Forest's unofficial starting offensive line is left tackle Tolu Olajide, left guard Clinton Richard, center Will Way, right guard Ryan Berger and right tackle Aidan Martin.
